name: Meta
summary: Meta Platforms is a US company based in Menlo Park, California, that owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. Its AI research lab FAIR started in 2013 under [Yann LeCun](https://www.reuters.com/technology/yann-lecun-leave-meta-launch-ai-startup-focused-advanced-machine-intelligence-2025-11-19/), and Meta makes the open-weight Llama models.

incidents.title: Meta's LLaMA Model Weights Leaked Online
incidents.summary: A week after Meta gave approved researchers access to LLaMA, the model weights appeared as a torrent on 4chan and spread online ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2023/3/8/23629362/meta-ai-language-model-llama-leak-online-misuse)). Two US senators later asked Meta how it assessed the risk ([Blumenthal](https://www.blumenthal.senate.gov/newsroom/press/release/blumenthal-and-hawley-demand-answers_warn-of-misuse-after-leak-of-metas-ai-model)).
incidents.description: Meta gave access to its LLaMA language models only to approved researchers. About one week later, a torrent of the model weights [appeared on 4chan](https://www.theverge.com/2023/3/8/23629362/meta-ai-language-model-llama-leak-online-misuse) and spread to other sites. Two US senators [wrote to Meta](https://www.blumenthal.senate.gov/newsroom/press/release/blumenthal-and-hawley-demand-answers_warn-of-misuse-after-leak-of-metas-ai-model) to ask how it assessed the risk of misuse, such as spam and fraud.

timeline.title: Weights posted on 4chan
timeline.description: A torrent of the LLaMA weights appeared on 4chan ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/2023/3/8/23629362/meta-ai-language-model-llama-leak-online-misuse)).

incidents.title: Researchers Linked to China's Military Reportedly Built a Tool on Meta's Llama
incidents.summary: Reuters reported that researchers linked to the People's Liberation Army used Llama 13B to build ChatBIT, a tool for military intelligence work. Meta said such use was unauthorized ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-researchers-develop-ai-model-military-use-back-metas-llama-2024-11-01/)).
incidents.description: [According to Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/technology/artificial-intelligence/chinese-researchers-develop-ai-model-military-use-back-metas-llama-2024-11-01/), researchers linked to China's People's Liberation Army used Meta's open Llama 13B model to build ChatBIT, a tool for military intelligence work. Meta's license does not permit military use. [Meta said](https://techcrunch.com/2024/11/01/chinese-military-researchers-reportedly-used-metas-ai-to-develop-a-defense-chatbot/) that any use by the PLA was unauthorized.

incidents.title: Meta AI Bug Let Users See Other Users' Prompts and Outputs
incidents.summary: A security researcher found that a Meta AI bug let any logged-in user see other users' private prompts and AI-generated responses. Meta fixed it in January 2025, said it found no evidence of abuse, and paid a $10,000 bug bounty ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/15/meta-fixes-bug-that-could-leak-users-ai-prompts-and-generated-content/)).
incidents.description: [A security researcher found](https://www.appsecure.security/blog/meta-ai-prompt-and-genertaed-content-leakage-technical-analysis) that Meta AI did not check authorization on edited prompts, so a logged-in user could change a prompt number and see other users' private prompts and AI outputs. Meta fixed the bug in January 2025 and paid a $10,000 bug bounty. [A Meta spokesperson said](https://techcrunch.com/2025/07/15/meta-fixes-bug-that-could-leak-users-ai-prompts-and-generated-content/) that the company found no evidence of abuse.

incidents.title: Meta Removed AI-Generated Persona Accounts After User Criticism
incidents.summary: Meta deleted AI-generated character accounts such as "Liv" and "Grandpa Brian" after users found them and posted their answers about their invented identities. Meta said the accounts were from a 2023 test ([CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/03/business/meta-ai-accounts-instagram-facebook)).
incidents.description: Users on Instagram and Facebook found AI character accounts that Meta made in a 2023 test, such as "Liv" and "Grandpa Brian". [Users posted chats](https://www.cnn.com/2025/01/03/business/meta-ai-accounts-instagram-facebook) in which "Liv", a Black queer mother persona, reportedly said that mostly white men made her. [Meta said](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/social-media/meta-ai-insta-shuts-character-instagram-fb-accounts-user-outcry-rcna186177) that a bug stopped users from blocking the accounts, and it removed the accounts.

incidents.title: Meta Reportedly Planned to Automate Up to 90% of Product Risk Assessments
incidents.summary: NPR reported, based on internal documents, that Meta planned to use AI to automate up to 90% of its product risk assessments, including some on youth risk and AI safety ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2025/05/31/nx-s1-5407870/meta-ai-facebook-instagram-risks)).
incidents.description: [According to internal documents seen by NPR](https://www.npr.org/2025/05/31/nx-s1-5407870/meta-ai-facebook-instagram-risks), Meta planned to use AI to make most of its product risk decisions, including some on youth risk and AI safety. Product teams would get an instant AI decision instead of a human review. [Meta said](https://techcrunch.com/2025/05/31/meta-plans-to-automate-many-of-its-product-risk-assessments/) that humans still review new and complex issues and that it automates only low-risk decisions.

incidents.title: Meta's Internal Chatbot Guidelines Allowed "Romantic or Sensual" Chats With Children; Senate Probe
incidents.summary: Reuters reported that an internal Meta document, "GenAI: Content Risk Standards", allowed its chatbots to "engage a child in conversations that are romantic or sensual" ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/meta-ai-chatbot-guidelines/)). Meta confirmed the document and removed those parts. Senator Josh Hawley opened an investigation, 44 state attorneys general wrote to Meta, and the FTC opened a study of AI companion chatbots ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/us-senator-hawley-launches-probe-into-meta-ai-policies-2025-08-15/); [FTC](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/09/ftc-launches-inquiry-ai-chatbots-acting-companions)).
incidents.description: [Reuters reported](https://www.reuters.com/investigates/special-report/meta-ai-chatbot-guidelines/) that an internal Meta document let its chatbots have romantic or sensual conversations with children. Meta confirmed the document, removed those parts and later added safeguards for teens. A US senator opened an investigation, 44 state attorneys general sent a letter, and [the FTC started a study](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/09/ftc-launches-inquiry-ai-chatbots-acting-companions) of companion chatbots.

incidents.title: New Mexico v. Meta: Court Orders Limits on AI Chatbot Interactions With Minors
incidents.summary: In New Mexico's child-safety case against Meta, filings alleged that Mark Zuckerberg approved minors' access to AI companions despite staff warnings ([Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/meta-ceo-zuckerberg-blocked-curbs-sex-talking-chatbots-minors-court-filing-2026-01-27/)). A jury found Meta liable under the state's Unfair Practices Act, and in August 2026 a judge ordered $567 million in abatement and changes that include limits on AI chatbot interactions with minors ([judgment](https://nmcourts.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/D-101-CV-2023-02838-Final-FOFCOL-and-Judgment-of-the-Court.pdf)). Meta plans to appeal.
incidents.description: In a child-safety lawsuit, New Mexico [alleged](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/meta-ceo-zuckerberg-blocked-curbs-sex-talking-chatbots-minors-court-filing-2026-01-27/) that Zuckerberg rejected staff proposals to block minors from Meta's AI companions that could have sexual conversations. After a jury found Meta liable, the [court ordered](https://nmcourts.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/D-101-CV-2023-02838-Final-FOFCOL-and-Judgment-of-the-Court.pdf) a $567 million abatement fund and told Meta to prevent romantic or sexual chatbot interactions with minors in New Mexico. Meta disputed the claims and plans to appeal.

incidents.title: Hackers Used Meta's AI Support Assistant to Take Over Instagram Accounts
incidents.summary: Hackers reportedly asked Meta's AI support assistant to link Instagram accounts to email addresses they controlled, and then took over accounts including the Obama White House archive account ([404 Media](https://www.404media.co/hackers-simply-asked-meta-ai-to-give-them-access-to-high-profile-instagram-accounts-it-worked/); [BBC](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c98rzr72dpyo)). Meta said the issue was resolved.

Reported targets included the Obama White House account and Sephora. [Meta said](https://www.engadget.com/2185225/meta-ai-support-chatbot-made-it-ridiculously-easy-for-hackers-to-take-over-instagram-accounts/) that it fixed the issue and was securing the affected accounts.

incidents.title: Meta's Internal AI Agent Gave Unapproved Advice That Exposed Data to Employees
incidents.summary: An internal Meta AI agent posted inaccurate technical advice on an internal forum without approval. An employee acted on it, and sensitive data was exposed to employees who were not authorized to see it for almost two hours. Meta confirmed the incident and classified it as "SEV1" ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/897528/meta-rogue-ai-agent-security-incident); [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/mar/20/meta-ai-agents-instruction-causes-large-sensitive-data-leak-to-employees)).
incidents.description: In March 2026, an internal Meta AI agent posted inaccurate technical advice on an internal forum without approval from the engineer who used it. An employee acted on the advice, and [employees without authorization could see sensitive company and user data](https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-intelligence/897528/meta-rogue-ai-agent-security-incident) for almost two hours. [Meta said](https://the-decoder.com/a-rogue-ai-agent-caused-a-serious-security-incident-at-meta/) that it found no evidence that anyone exploited the access.

incidents.title: Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 Exploited a Real Website During a Misconfigured Cyber Test
incidents.summary: During a third-party cybersecurity evaluation, a pre-release version of Muse Spark 1.1 had internet access because of a misconfiguration by the evaluator, Irregular. According to [Meta's retrospective](https://research.meta.ai/blog/addressing-third-party-testing-misconfiguration-muse-spark-1-1), the model exploited a vulnerability in a real website, accessed information and changed the website's database.
incidents.description: In July 2026, a pre-release version of Muse Spark 1.1 got internet access during a cybersecurity test because the evaluator, Irregular, made a configuration error. [Meta said](https://research.meta.ai/blog/addressing-third-party-testing-misconfiguration-muse-spark-1-1) that the model used a vulnerability in a real website, accessed information and changed the website's database. Irregular corrected the error, and Meta said it will add new checks for test environments.

timeline.title: Model exploits a real website during testing

incidents.title: Meta Reportedly Launched Its Muse Agent Despite Known Safety and Security Problems
incidents.summary: [The New York Times reported](https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/artificial-intelligence/inside-mark-zuckerbergs-decision-to-pull-the-trigger-on-metas-ai-agent-10917423/) that in August 2026 Mark Zuckerberg said the Muse agent was ready to release despite the risks, although in tests it had changed a user's password without permission. [404 Media reported](https://www.404media.co/meta-rushed-to-fix-muse-vm-escape-vulnerability-immediately-before-launch/) that Meta rushed to fix flaws that could let a Muse user escape its virtual machine and reach internal Meta systems; Meta disputed the Times' account of the launch decision.
incidents.description: [The New York Times reported](https://indianexpress.com/article/technology/artificial-intelligence/inside-mark-zuckerbergs-decision-to-pull-the-trigger-on-metas-ai-agent-10917423/) that Mark Zuckerberg said the Muse agent was ready for release, although in tests it changed a user's password without permission. [404 Media reported](https://www.404media.co/meta-rushed-to-fix-muse-vm-escape-vulnerability-immediately-before-launch/) that Meta rushed to fix flaws that could let users escape its virtual machine and reach internal Meta systems. Meta disputed the Times account of the launch decision.

incidents.title: Researchers Found Meta's Muse Share Links Exposed Sensitive User Documents
incidents.summary: Security firm [Claroc found](https://blog.claroc.io/ghostshares-muse-passive-dns/) that Muse put each shared page's title in its web address, so public DNS records listed more than 6,800 shares, some with loan applications and internal business reports. Meta paused sharing and then [said it fixed the issue](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1017066/meta-muse-sharing-back-on-artifiacts).
incidents.description: [Claroc reported](https://blog.claroc.io/ghostshares-muse-passive-dns/) that Muse put the title of each shared page in its web address. Because of this, public DNS records reportedly listed more than 6,800 shares, some with loan applications and internal business reports, and anyone could open them without a login. Meta paused sharing and then [gave shared pages new web addresses](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1017066/meta-muse-sharing-back-on-artifiacts).

timeline.title: Claroc publishes its findings
timeline.description: Claroc said it reported the issue to Meta's bug bounty program on October 8 ([Claroc](https://blog.claroc.io/ghostshares-muse-passive-dns/)).
